decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit is a core, flagship extension of the firm's airfield lighting business with long airport lifecycles, so its option value is high and keeping it costs little.

The air situation display complements the tower and surveillance portfolio and costs little to maintain as software, so keeping it open is cheaper than abandoning it while demand recovers after the pandemic.
The airport systems training program is a low-cost service tied to the installed base, and pandemic disruption has not yet revealed its true value, so it stays.
The AGL training course was only mentioned and not featured, but it serves the core lighting business at negligible carrying cost, so it should be kept or merged into broader training.
Collaboration software is central to the firm's integrated, data-driven strategy, and its uncertainty is still unresolved after the downturn in air traffic, so the option should be held.
The MLAT system extends the surveillance offering with long procurement cycles, so its prospects remain uncertain but valuable, which justifies keeping it rather than abandoning it.
